name: MASTERSPIKE
description: The elected Master's knowledge manifest, in the three-layer llm-wiki shape: raw sources, the distilled wiki, and the schema that governs both. Every layer is oriented to administration — this is the knowledge an admin surface reasons over, not a peer's working knowledge.
not_a_model_choice: This manifest names layers, not a base model. Which model serves the admin surface is a separate, unmade decision, and writing one in here would imply a choice nobody has made.

raw.what_belongs_here: Everything authoritative that has not yet been distilled: cluster trust roots, signed registry entries, ledger blocks, contract revisions, unit files, the plans, and the raw session transcripts that explain why a decision was taken.
raw.authority: Authoritative but poor to query directly — this layer is the source code, not the running program.

authoritative.why: The narrative contract for election, roots and re-formation, including the open question about losing a member.
Defines identity_fields and cluster_trust_root once, for both roles.
The capability vocabulary, trust levels and share clocks. A grant is meaningless outside it.
Every port either role binds or dials, with implementation_state separated from runtime.
The hash-chained record. Proves integrity and order; does not prove truth.
The fail-closed template. As shipped it names no Master and carries no signatures.
The declared admin topology, including the capability this surface is not allowed.
The work order and its current cursor.
Three units. The signer unit is staged but never enabled by make units.

raw.ingest_note: Raw material is captured, never deleted from _raw/. Ingest moves and distils; it does not discard the only copy.

wiki.vault_path_source: master-node/.env (VAULT_PATH) — never hard-coded in a page
wiki.what_belongs_here: Distilled, cross-referenced knowledge an admin can answer from without re-deriving it: how authority works, what each key signs, what a re-formation costs, what the ledger does and does not prove, what the boundaries are and why.

core_pages.answers: Why three Ed25519 keys, and which one signs what.
Why a deployment directory confers nothing and a node is a peer until elected.
Why the signer is a separate process and not a permission rule.
What a hash chain proves, and the thing it does not.
Why absence of a Master ratification is not evidence of absence.
What the admin surface may reach, and the one capability it may not.
What follows from unanimity at n=3, drawn across the protocol, the signer and the recovery story.

wiki.provenance: Every page carries a provenance state. A claim with no source is marked a guess, and a guess is allowed to be wrong in public — an unsourced assertion is not.
wiki.query_before_crawl: An admin surface that re-derives what the wiki already answers will drift from it, and drift in a knowledge base is invisible until it is expensive.

schema.what_belongs_here: The rules that govern how the other two layers are maintained: what an admin claim must cite, how a verdict is worded, which states a page may claim, and what must never be written down.

rules.three_states_only: A component is specified, implemented-and-tested, or deployed. No fourth state, and no blending — 'basically working' is how a signer that has never signed anything ends up described as live.
rules.cite_or_mark: Every factual claim carries a path or a ledger block. Without one it is labelled a guess.
rules.no_secrets: Keys are referenced by path only, never by value. This is the single rule with the worst possible failure mode.
rules.specification_is_not_implementation: Now that this role has code, the risk runs the other way: describing the signer or the election as working when neither is deployed.
rules.one_copy_of_a_contract: Contracts live in contracts/ and are implemented once in shared/. A role that restates one creates drift, and drift in a signature-verifying path shows up as a node that verifies on one machine and not another.
rules.negative_results_belong: A question the fabric cannot answer is a finding. Record it as an open question rather than smoothing over it — the re-formation paradox exists in the contract precisely because it was written down instead of being quietly assumed away.
rules.verdicts_are_graded: Supported, Contradicted, Unproven, Out of scope. 'Unproven' is never reported as 'did not happen'.

schema.enforcement: master-node/tests/ — spec and prose-truth tests fail the build on a claim the code does not support. A rule nothing checks is a preference.
